shortDescription: The South African rand weakened on Wednesday, shrugging off stronger-than-expected retail sales data and stable inflation expectations as investors waited to hear the U.S. Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision.

children: The South African rand weakened on Wednesday, shrugging off stronger-than-expected retail sales data and stable inflation expectations as investors waited to hear the U.S. Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision.
At 1450 GMT, the rand traded at 16.28 against the dollar
firmed against a basket of currencies.
Market participants are betting heavily that Fed policymakers will lift their benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point, to a 3.75%-4% range, and signal further tightening ahead.

Analysts said the rand could remain volatile in the near term, as, like other risk-sensitive currencies, it is influenced by global factors such as U.S. economic data and monetary policy, alongside domestic developments.

South African inflation expectations stabilised in the third quarter, a survey showed on Wednesday, after a steep rise in the previous quarter because of the oil price shock triggered by the Iran war.
The quarterly survey is commissioned by the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) and guides its thinking on the appropriate level of interest rates.

"This is very encouraging. While most of the expectations did not decline to levels seen in the first quarter, they were down from the second-quarter survey numbers," said Johann Els, chief economist at PSG Financial Services.
Els said he expects the SARB to leave interest rates unchanged at its policy meeting next week.

Separate data from Statistics South Africa showed retail sales rose 3.4% year on year in July, accelerating from a revised 1.1% increase in June. Analysts polled by Reuters expected sales to rise 0.9%.
On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) strengthened, with the yield down 7.5 basis points to 8.735%.
